schema: shared-bodies/v1. The heavy markdown bodies spelled twice - in Go, as the Shapes and NestedDirectives of packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/pmdoc/heavybodies, and in TypeScript, as the exports of packages/dispatch/e2e/heavy-bodies.ts - and the bodies only one of the two has. A shared row names a body both sides spell: its id (a Shape's or NestedDirective's ID, and the key of heavy-bodies.ts's heavyBodies record), the Go name it carries, the TypeScript export it is, its length in bytes (UTF-8, what Go's len over the body counts) and the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of those bytes, taken for a Shape at full size (Shape.Grow). A oneSideOnly row names a body one side has alone: its id, that side, and why the other does not spell it. Every body a side spells stands exactly once across the two lists, so a body added, dropped, renamed or respelled on one side alone fails that side's reader: heavybodies/digests_test.go here, and packages/dispatch/e2e/__tests__/heavy-bodies-digests.test.ts there.

shared.goName: a quote then lines carrying no marker
a run of 15,000 brackets and as many closers
100 items nested by indentation then blank lines
a chain of 15,999 list markers on one line
a typed fence whose label opens a run of brackets
2,000 unclosed openers then a long line

oneSideOnly.why: Go's Shape "49 items nested by indentation then blank lines" writes one item per line, 49 lines growing from 4 to 100 characters, and no spec of packages/dispatch/e2e has ever written that body. Go's other 49-block shape, markers-49-then-blank-lines, writes the same 98 blocks on one line: the two are stored alike but are different bytes and cost the parser different things, so Go keeps both. What gates this one is pmdoc's TestHeavyBodiesAtTheBlockCapAreStoredOrRefusedInTime and the API's TestHeavyDocumentWriteVerdicts.

Go's Shape "a list item then lines carrying no marker" was spelled in packages/dispatch/e2e/heavy-bodies.ts too, as that module's lazyListItem, for the document writes the deleted heavy-document-writes.e2e.ts made through the API (INFRA-1404). No browser row draws the body - heavy-bodies.e2e.ts's lazy row is lazyQuote - so the browser suite no longer spells it. What gates it is pmdoc's TestHeavyBodiesAtTheBlockCapAreStoredOrRefusedInTime and the API's TestHeavyDocumentWriteVerdicts.

Go's Shape "49 list markers on one line then blank lines" was heavy-bodies.ts's nested49ThenBlankLines, which only the deleted heavy-document-writes.e2e.ts drew (INFRA-1404). heavy-bodies.e2e.ts's own 49-marker row builds its body inline, 49 markers padded to one character under the parse worker's threshold rather than to the 32,000-character body cap, so that is a different body and not this one respelled. What gates this one is pmdoc's TestHeavyBodiesAtTheBlockCapAreStoredOrRefusedInTime and the API's TestHeavyDocumentWriteVerdicts.

heavy-bodies.ts's nestedThenTextLines - 100 items nested by indentation, then lines of text rather than blank lines - is drawn in the browser only (heavy-bodies.e2e.ts). No Shape spells it, and none of the document-write rows this change moved into Go wrote it, so Go would be gating a body no writer here sends.
